reason: Two independent dogfood runs reproduced the same forbidden lifecycle state: the canonical next action can be a command that cannot advance the blocker it names. The repository has since hardened this with release-set recovery-convergence assertions and a continuous F-GATE. Promote that existing executable enforcement into the reviewed Constraint lineage instead of adding another soft reminder or duplicate test.
remaining_uncertainty: This proposal intentionally adopts existing CI enforcement. The owner-side generation/activation path still has to prove that an already-existing hard constraint can be promoted without generating a duplicate implementation.
scope_justification: The two source findings directly cover RunPolicyEvaluator. The release-set runner and F-GATE workflow are the current hard enforcement added after those observations; including them is necessary to bind the durable Constraint to the executable guard that now owns the invariant.

constraint.violation: A recovery result advertises a canonical next action that cannot advance or change the blocking state, causing an obedient host to repeat the same state/action indefinitely.
allowed_boundaries: decision_required may remain non-mutating because progress requires explicit judgment rather than a mechanical repair
host_work may require model work, but it must name the owner/cause/action needed to change the state rather than a read-only diagnostic loop
